```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), ".."))   # analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations -> analysis
os.chdir("..")                                # -> twogroup_experiments/
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 110
import polars as pl
import laplacelib as R
import pip_agreement as P

comp, fits, feat = P.load()
cn, fn = comp.filter(~pl.col("null")), fits.filter(~pl.col("null"))
cd = cn.filter(pl.col("declared_ref") | pl.col("declared_arm"))   # pairs at least one side declares (Means section)
```

Every arm is compared with CAVI-Q2 on the same replicate. For single effect $l$,
$\alpha_l$ is the posterior over which feature carries the effect: $\alpha_l =
\text{softmax}(\log \text{BF}_l)$ under the uniform prior. Three distances between CAVI-Q2's
$\alpha$ and the arm's $\alpha'$:

- $\text{TV} = \tfrac12 \sum_j |\alpha_j - \alpha'_j|$, the largest change in the probability of
  any set of features (a credible set is one).
- $\text{KL}(\alpha \,\|\, \alpha') = \sum_j \alpha_j \log(\alpha_j / \alpha'_j)$, in nats,
  computed from log BFs (no floor). Large when the arm puts little mass where CAVI-Q2 has mass.
  It is the variable-selection term of the KL between the two single-effect posteriors.
- $\max_j |\alpha_j - \alpha'_j|$, the largest single-feature change (TV over single features).

At $L = 5$ the components are unordered, so each arm's components are matched to CAVI-Q2's by
minimum total TV. At both $L$, a component pair counts only if at least one side declares it
(component $\log \text{BF} \ge 2$); null components have diffuse $\alpha$ and their distances
are noise. The last table is per fit and needs no matching: $\max_j |\text{PIP}_j -
\text{PIP}'_j|$ over the combined PIPs. At $L = 1$ it equals $\max |\Delta\alpha|$ wherever a
component is declared.

Designs: *Binary* (binary Markov sets, experiment 022), *Binary-Block* (nested binary blocks,
024) and *Gaussian* (Gaussian AR(1), 023). Fits: the full grids at L=5 and the `-ser` grids at
L=1, 200 replicates each. Non-null cells only.

```{python}
#| label: status
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
st = (P.with_design(fn).group_by("design", "L", maintain_order=True)
      .agg(pl.col("batch_hash").n_unique().alias("batches"),
           (pl.len() / pl.col("method").n_unique()).cast(pl.Int64).alias("reps"),
           pl.col("n_pairs").mean().alias("pairs")).sort("design", "L"))
for r in st.iter_rows(named=True):
    print(f"- {r['design']}, L={r['L']}: {r['batches']} batches, {r['reps']} paired replicates per arm, "
          f"{r['pairs']:.2f} declared component pairs per fit")
```

```{python}
#| label: helpers
#| include: false
def table(df, value, legend, digits=3):
    tab = P.fmt(P.summarize(P.with_design(df), value, ["design", "L", "method"]), digits)
    print(R.md_table(tab, rows=["design", "L"], value="cell", fmt="{}", legend=legend))

COMMON = ("*design*: simulated design (Binary, Binary-Block, Gaussian). "
          "*L*: fitted components. Each arm column: mean over {unit}, with a 95% interval from "
          "resampling replicates. 0 = identical to CAVI-Q2.")
```


## Per replicate {#sec-per-rep}

A small mean distance can come from every replicate being close or from most replicates being
identical and a few far apart. To tell these apart, take one number per fit, $\max_j
|\text{PIP}_j - \text{PIP}'_j|$, the largest PIP change over all 256 features, and look at
its distribution over replicates. It needs no component matching.

```{python}
#| label: tab-pip-quantiles
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(R.md_table(P.with_design(P.quantile_cells(fn)), rows=["design", "L"], value="cell", fmt="{}",
      legend="*design*: simulated design (Binary, Binary-Block, Gaussian). "
             "*L*: fitted components. Each arm column: median / 90th / 99th percentile over fits "
             "(non-null cells, every replicate) of the largest absolute PIP difference from "
             "CAVI-Q2 on the same replicate."))
```

```{python}
#| label: tab-pip-shares
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(R.md_table(P.with_design(P.share_cells(fn)), rows=["design", "L"], value="cell", fmt="{}",
      legend="Columns as above. Each arm column: share of fits whose largest absolute PIP "
             "difference from CAVI-Q2 is at most 0.01 / above 0.1."))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-pip-survival
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Share of fits whose largest PIP difference from CAVI-Q2 exceeds x (non-null cells). Dotted lines at 0.01 and 0.1; values below 1e-4 are drawn at 1e-4."
P.survival_figure(fn);
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-pip-scatter
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "L = 5: each feature's PIP under the arm against CAVI-Q2, pooled over replicates and non-null cells; colour is the log count per hexagon. Features with both PIPs below 0.05 (most of them) are left out."
P.scatter_figure(feat, 5);
```


### Matched alphas {#sec-matched}

Matching each arm component to a CAVI-Q2 component (minimum total TV, exact over all
assignments) lets the two fits be compared component by component. For each matched pair, the
total variation $\text{TV} = \tfrac12\sum_j |\alpha_{lj} - \alpha'_{s(l)j}|$ is the largest
change in the mass of any feature set, so it bounds how much a credible set's mass can move.
The matching minimizes total TV, so these are the smallest TVs any one-to-one pairing gives.
The first row uses every matched pair, with no log BF threshold; the others keep pairs whose
smaller component log BF exceeds a bar (both sides must clear it).

```{python}
#| label: fig-bar-l5
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "L = 5: share of matched pairs whose TV exceeds x (1 - CDF), for all pairs and for pairs whose smaller component log BF exceeds 0, 1, 2 (non-null cells). Dotted lines at 0.01 and 0.1."
P.survival_figure(cn, rows=P.bar_rows(5), xlabel="TV, matched pair", unit="pairs");
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-bar-l1
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "L = 1: as above, one component per fit."
P.survival_figure(cn, rows=P.bar_rows(1), xlabel="TV, single effect", unit="pairs");
```

### When gIBSS and CAVI-Q2 disagree {#sec-tail}

The fits in the tail are mostly different optima of the same objective. The table splits fits by
their largest PIP difference and compares the Q2 ELBO, which CAVI-Q2 maximizes directly, so a
small deficit for the gIBSS arms is expected even at the same optimum.

```{python}
#| label: tab-tail
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(P.md_frame(P.tail_table(fn), {"median ΔELBO": "{:+.3f}", "CAVI-Q2 higher": "{:.1%}",
                                    "arm higher": "{:.1%}", "declared count differs": "{:.1%}"},
      legend="*band*: the fit's largest absolute PIP difference from CAVI-Q2. *fits*: fits in the "
             "band (non-null cells). *median ΔELBO*: median of arm Q2 ELBO minus CAVI-Q2's, in "
             "nats. *CAVI-Q2 higher* / *arm higher*: share of fits where that side's ELBO is "
             "higher by more than 0.1 nat. *declared count differs*: share of fits where the two "
             "sides declare a different number of components (log BF >= 2)."))
```


```{python}
#| label: fig-worst
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "The four L = 5 replicates with the largest gIBSS-Q2 PIP difference from CAVI-Q2. Left CAVI-Q2, right gIBSS-Q2, same replicate; coloured points are declared 95% credible sets, gIBSS-Q2 components coloured by their CAVI-Q2 match; ringed features with vertical lines are the causal features. x is cropped to the features with any PIP. PIPs include undeclared components, which carry no colour: in the third row the CAVI-Q2 PIP of 0.89 near feature 21 comes from an undeclared component."
worst = (fn.filter((pl.col("method") == "gibss") & (pl.col("L") == 5))
         .sort("max_pip", descending=True).head(4).to_dicts())
P.replicate_figure(worst);
```
